Steps: Open /project/create; reach Terms and visibility; inspect the application access control.
Expected Result: Control is visible, defaults to Active GO members only, and explains that free users can apply only when all signed-in users are allowed.
Preconditions: Logged-in project creator

Steps: Create or edit a project; choose All signed-in users, including free users; save; refresh the project and edit form.
Expected Result: The broader application policy saves and remains selected after refresh; the project detail copy reflects the setting.
Preconditions: Hiring project owned by the test account

Steps: As a signed-in free user, open a hiring project configured for all signed-in users and submit an application.
Expected Result: Application is created successfully once; no paid membership prompt blocks the flow.
Feature: Free user applies to opted-in project
Preconditions: Free account; public hiring project with applicationAccess set to all_signed_in_users

Steps: As a paid member, apply to one members-only project and one all-signed-in-users project.
Expected Result: Both applications are accepted under their respective policies.
Feature: Paid member applies under both policies
Preconditions: Active Community or Business account; two hiring projects with different policies

Steps: As a project admin who is not the creator, open the edit form and attempt to change who may apply; also attempt the direct update request.
Expected Result: The control is read-only and the direct update is rejected; other permitted project edits remain unaffected.
Feature: Project admin cannot change application policy
Preconditions: Admin access to another user's project; separate API request capability

Steps: Open an older project with no applicationAccess value; inspect its detail page and attempt application as a free user.
Expected Result: The project displays and enforces Active GO members only, preserving legacy behavior.
Preconditions: Legacy hiring project without applicationAccess field

Steps: As an anonymous visitor, open a hiring project configured for all signed-in users and click Apply.
Expected Result: Visitor is prompted to sign in; no application is created before authentication.
Preconditions: Public hiring project with all-signed-in-users policy

Steps: Attempt to apply to private, invite-only, or non-hiring projects under both application policies.
Expected Result: Visibility and hiring-status rules still reject the application regardless of the selected applicant policy.
Feature: Application policy does not bypass project access rules
Preconditions: Test projects covering private/invite-only and non-hiring states

Steps: Send direct application requests as a free user to members-only and all-signed-in-users projects; send an unauthorized policy update as a non-owner admin.
Expected Result: The server enforces the stored policy and rejects the unauthorized policy update; UI restrictions cannot be bypassed through the API.
Preconditions: Authenticated test tokens; projects with both policies

Steps: Change a project from members-only to all-signed-in-users and inspect an existing application before and after the change.
Expected Result: Existing application status and applicant data are unchanged; the new policy applies only to future applications.
Preconditions: Project with an existing application and creator access
